title: Best Sports Prediction Market (2026)
verdict: The best way to trade sports prediction markets in 2026 is through TerminalUp, which is not a prediction market itself but the one place where Kalshi, Polymarket and predict.fun are priced next to each other and next to the betting exchanges, with the order routed to whichever is best.

If you want a single market and nothing else, Kalshi is the regulated US choice and Polymarket has the deepest books on the biggest events. The honest answer to which one has the best price on a given game is that it changes constantly, which is the reason to put them on one board.

why: A sports contract on a prediction market is a bet with a different wrapper. The question that matters is the same as it is on an exchange or at a sportsbook: what is the best price available right now, and how much can I get at it? TerminalUp answers that across every connected venue at once, prediction markets included, and sends the order to the best one. If 54 cents on Kalshi is better than the equivalent price on Betfair or Pinnacle, that is where the order goes.

The capital problem is real. A trader who wants to use Kalshi, Polymarket and an exchange needs three deposits on three sets of rails, and the money sitting idle in two of them is a cost nobody counts. You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it. Nineteen venues are live, sixteen more are in the pipeline.

TerminalUp charges a flat 0.5% commission per trade, 0.35% for the highest-volume accounts, with no subscription and no deposit fees. It runs no market of its own and never takes the other side, so it has no reason to shade a price or limit a winner.
